content: श्री €9 <ab>U.</ab> (श्रीणाति, श्रीणीते) .²1 To cook, dress, boil, prepare. .²2 To diffuse light; श्रीणन्नुप स्थाद् दिवं भुरण्युः <ls>Rv. 1. 68. 1</ls>.

श्री {%f.%} [श्रि-क्विप् नि˚ <ls>Uṇ. 2. 57</ls>] .²1 Wealth, riches, affluence, prosperity, plenty; अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलम् <ls>Rām.</ls>; साहसे श्रीः प्रतिवसति <ls>Mk. 4</ls> ‘fortune favours the brave’; कर्माण्यारभमाणं हि पुरुषं श्रीर्निषेवते <ls>Ms. 9. 300</ls>; <ls>Ki. 7. 28</ls>. .²2 Royalty, majesty, royal wealth; श्रियः कुरूणामधिपस्य पालनीम् <ls>Ki. 1. 1</ls>. .²3 Dignity, high position, state; श्रीलक्षण <ls>Ku. 7. 45</ls> ‘the marks or insignia of greatness or dignity’; दुराराध्याः श्रियो राज्ञां दुरापा दुष्परिग्रहाः <ls>Pt. 1. 67</ls>; विद्युल्लेखाकनकरुचिरं श्रीवितानं ममाभ्रम् <ls>V. 4. 13</ls>. .²4 Beauty, grace, splendour, lustre; (मुखं) कमलश्रियं दधौ <ls>Ku. 5. 21</ls>, <ls n="Ku.">7. 32</ls>; <ls>R. 3. 8</ls>. .²5 Colour, aspect; तेषामाविरभूद् ब्रह्मा परिम्लानमुखश्रियाम् <ls>Ku. 2. 2</ls>. .²6 The goddess of wealth, Laksmī, the wife of Viṣṇu; आसीदियं दशरथस्य गृहे यथा श्रीः <ls>U. 4. 6</ls>; <ls>Ś. 3. 14</ls>; <ls>Śi. 1. 1</ls>. .²7 Any virtue or excellence. .²8 Decoration. .²9 Intellect, understanding. .²10 Superhuman power. .²11 The three objects of human existence taken collectively (धर्म, अर्थ and काम). .²12 The Sarala tree. .²13 The Bilva tree. .²14 Cloves. .²15 A lotus. .²16 The twelfth digit of the moon. .²17 <ab>N.</ab> of Sarasvatī, (the goddess of speech). .²18 Speech. .²19 Fame, glory. .²20 The three Vedas (वेदत्रयी); श्रिया विहीनैरधनैर्नास्तिकैः संप्रवर्तितम् <ls>Mb. 12. 10. 20</ls> (‘ऋचः सामानि यजूंषि . सा हि श्रीरमृता सताम्’ इति श्रुतेः . <ab>com.</ab>). --{%m.%} <ab>N.</ab> of one of the six {%Rāgas%} or musical modes. --{%a.%} Splendid, radiant, adorning. (The word श्री is often used as an honorific prefix to the names of deities and eminent persons; श्रीकृष्णः, श्रीरामः, श्रीवाल्मीकिः, श्रीजयदेवः; also celebrated works, generally of a sacred character; श्रीभागवत, श्रीरामायण <ab>&c.</ab>; it is also used as an auspicious sign at the commencement of letters, manuscripts <ab>&c.</ab>; Māgha has used this word in the last stanza of each canto of his Śiśupālavadha, as Bhāravi has used लक्ष्मी).
